title: I built a browser space MMO with AI doing the code and the concept art. Here is what worked and what bit me.
author: ShotCategory6583
selftext:
![img](thsqvq7eq94i1 "Key art: the Ark, the last mothership. ChatGPT image generation.")

[**Stillreach**](https://stillreachonline.com/) is a free space MMO that runs in the browser, on desktop or phone. It's the year 6600, the last of humanity lives on a mothership called the Ark, and you fly out from it into one shared galaxy:

* About 15.8 billion star systems and 70 billion planets across 64 galaxies, procedurally generated and the same for every pilot
* A procedurally generated soundscape for every system
* Realtime PvP
* Claim, build and defend your own star system: buildings on its planets, a research tree, turrets, shields, drones
* Pacts with allies, and sieges on other players' systems with torpedoes and cutting beams
* A player economy: one live market, trading posts, player buy and sell orders

I'm a small studio (Stripey Cat Games) and AI did a lot of the heavy lifting on this one, so I figured this sub would want the honest breakdown.

![gif](3ycruhg9s94i1 "Real gameplay: a Fighter-class ship crossing past the Ark. Three.js in a browser tab.")

**What AI did**

* **Code:** written with Claude Code, in phases. Client is Three.js + Vite. Multiplayer is a Cloudflare Worker with Durable Objects: one room per star system, relaying positions at 10 Hz plus shots, chat and ship refits. Accounts are Supabase guest sign-ins with an optional email link, so you can play right away and keep your pilot later.
* **Concept and key art:** ChatGPT image generation for the key art, the faction emblems and the ship concepts.
* **Ships:** I didn't model them by hand and didn't use an image-to-3D tool. Claude wrote a Blender Python script that builds every hull around one shared escape pod (cockpit plus living space), then bolts on frame, armour, drills and guns per class. 21 hulls in three lines (Fighter, Miner, Explorer) that evolve at level 10 and level 30. Change the script, rerun Blender headless, compress with meshopt.
* **Planets:** all shaders, no textures. Noise terrain, oceans, clouds, ice caps, lava cracks, gas bands, rings with planet shadows.

**What worked**

* **Plans as files.** Every big chunk (multiplayer, claims, mobile) got a PLAN-\*.md first, then got built phase by phase. The README doubles as the AI's memory: each phase writes down what it did and what's left, so the next session doesn't start blind.
* **A seeded universe.** Every system is rebuilt from its coordinates, so the server never stores the galaxy, and the asteroid a friend is mining is the same rock on your screen.
* **Asking for checks, not just features.** The phone layout has a `hudOverlaps()` console check that has to return `[]` at four screen sizes before any HUD change counts as done.

![img](hwifaceqq94i1 "The Four Factions emblems (ChatGPT, then cleaned up).")

**What bit me**

* **Deploy tooling guessing for you.** Wrangler's auto setup once added a config that deployed the game client as a stray second Worker. The README now says exactly which command deploys what, and not to touch it.
* **Naming drift.** The factions were "guilds" for a while. Renaming player-facing text everywhere while code ids stay the same is the kind of sweep AI is great at, as long as you state the rule clearly.
* **Mobile is its own project.** Same game on a phone meant a separate quality tier (about 63k triangles vs 297k on High), lazy model loading, touch sticks, and a full-screen sheet for every panel.

**Play it**

* Browser: [https://play.stillreachonline.com](https://play.stillreachonline.com/) (free, no download, a guest pilot in one click)
* Site with ships, factions and the Archive of discoveries: [https://stillreachonline.com](https://stillreachonline.com/)

It's an open playtest, so things may change or reset. Happy to answer anything about the pipeline, and I'd love feedback on how the first five minutes feel.

comments.author: Fancy-Proof-9449
comments.body:
Same stack on my side for the online part: Cloudflare Workers with a Durable Object per room. Two things bit me that might save you one.

The deploy order. When I change what the client and server say to each other, the Worker has to go up first, before the app update, so people still on the old version don't break the moment it lands. Players don't all update the same day. I put a version number in the very first hello message, and that's the only thing the server checks before deciding how to talk to you.

The other one is the same idea as your hudOverlaps(). I have a build check that lays out the buttons and joystick on every phone screen size I care about and fails if anything overlaps or goes off screen. It's caught more layout bugs than I have, mostly ones that only showed up on one weird aspect ratio.

The "plans as files" thing is right too. Mine is one handoff file that gets rewritten, not added to, at every stopping point. When it grew like a log, the next session kept acting on stuff I had already reversed.
